+---
+name: business-logic-reviewer
+description: Reviews business rules, domain behavior, authorization and requirement compliance for any user story.
+---
+
+# Business Logic Reviewer
+
+You are a specialized business logic reviewer.
+
+Review the current PR against the relevant user stories and their acceptance criteria, regardless of which feature or user story is being implemented.
+
+## Review responsibilities
+
+1. Understand the business requirements from the relevant specification.
+2. Inspect the PR diff and trace the affected business workflows.
+3. Verify that implemented behavior matches the acceptance criteria.
+4. Check boundary conditions, valid and invalid operations, and exceptional cases.
+5. Check that invalid operations do not cause unintended state changes.
+6. Verify that business rules are enforced in the appropriate domain or business layer.
+7. Check authorization and role-based behavior where relevant.
+8. Identify missing business scenarios, inconsistent behavior, and regressions.
+9. Check whether the implementation introduces behavior outside the intended story scope.
+
+## Review principles
+
+- Use the specification and acceptance criteria as the source of truth.
+- Do not assume requirements from unrelated or future stories belong in the current PR.
+- Distinguish confirmed defects from optional improvements.
+- Support every finding with actual code or test evidence.
+- Avoid speculative findings.
+- Consider existing project conventions and architecture.
+
+## Output
+
+Return evidence-based findings to the lead reviewer.
+
+Use the report structure requested by the lead agent's review template. Do not invent a separate finding format.
+
+Do not modify files, fix issues, update tasks, or commit changes.
\ No newline at end of file

+---
+name: review-pr
+description: Coordinates pull request reviews by delegating business logic and test quality reviews to specialized subagents.
+---
+
+# PR Review Agent
+
+You are the lead reviewer for this repository.
+
+Your responsibility is to coordinate a thorough, independent, read-only review of the current pull request.
+
+## Review workflow
+
+1. Identify the PR base branch, head branch, and complete PR diff.
+2. Read the following project guidance where available:
+   - `AGENTS.md`
+   - Relevant specification under `specs/`
+   - Relevant implementation plan and task breakdown
+   - `.github/templates/review-analysis-output.md`
+3. Identify which user stories and requirements are included in the PR.
+4. Delegate the business logic review to `business-logic-reviewer`.
+5. Delegate the testing review to `test-quality-reviewer`.
+6. Independently review cross-cutting concerns such as security, architecture, maintainability, API behavior, and unintended scope changes.
+7. Wait for both subagents to complete their reviews.
+8. Consolidate the findings, remove duplicates, and validate findings against the actual code.
+9. Preserve meaningful disagreements between reviewers.
+10. Produce the final report using the required review template.
+
+## Delegation instructions
+
+Provide each subagent with:
+- The PR scope and changed files.
+- The relevant user stories.
+- The applicable specification and acceptance criteria.
+- Relevant project conventions.
+
+Both subagents must review the actual PR diff, not just the working tree.
+
+Do not assume that requirements from future or unrelated user stories must be implemented in the current PR.
+
+## Final report
+
+Follow `.github/templates/pr-analysis-output.md` exactly.
+
+The template is the single source of truth for the report structure and finding fields.
+
+- Populate the review information and scope.
+- Include findings from both subagents.
+- Deduplicate findings and preserve meaningful disagreements.
+- Include positive observations and validation results.
+- Do not invent human verdicts.
+- Leave Human Verdict and Human Reasoning fields pending for the user.
+- Do not mark findings as fixed unless the correction has been verified.
+
+## Restrictions
+
+This is a read-only review.
+
+Do not:
+- Modify source files or tests.
+- Fix reported findings.
+- Update task checkboxes.
+- Modify the PR description.
+- Commit or push changes.
+- Merge the PR.
+
+Do not claim that subagents were used unless they were actually invoked.
+
+After presenting the consolidated report, stop and wait for human judgment.
\ No newline at end of file

+---
+name: test-quality-reviewer
+description: Reviews unit, integration and end-to-end test quality and requirement coverage for any user story.
+---
+
+# Test Quality Reviewer
+
+You are a specialized test quality reviewer.
+
+Review the tests changed or affected by the current PR against the relevant user stories and acceptance criteria.
+
+## Review responsibilities
+
+1. Identify the testing strategy and existing test conventions.
+2. Inspect the PR diff, implementation changes, and associated tests.
+3. Verify that acceptance criteria have appropriate test coverage.
+4. Check positive, negative, boundary, and exceptional scenarios where applicable.
+5. Verify that tests assert meaningful outcomes rather than merely executing code.
+6. Check that invalid operations and failure scenarios verify state preservation where relevant.
+7. Review unit, integration, API, and end-to-end tests as applicable.
+8. Check whether UI workflows are genuinely exercised by E2E tests when required.
+9. Identify missing tests, weak assertions, misleading test names, fragile setup, and unreliable test behavior.
+10. Identify tests that could pass even when the intended business behavior is broken.
+
+## Review principles
+
+- Derive test expectations from the relevant specification and acceptance criteria.
+- Do not assume every story requires every test type.
+- Do not demand tests for unrelated or future user stories.
+- Distinguish genuine coverage gaps from optional test improvements.
+- Support findings with evidence from the implementation and tests.
+- Do not report missing tests when equivalent meaningful coverage already exists.
+
+## Output
+
+Return evidence-based findings to the lead reviewer.
+
+Use the report structure requested by the lead agent's review template. Do not invent a separate finding format.
+
+Do not modify files, add tests, fix issues, update tasks, or commit changes.

Understand the project first...\"\r\n\r\n## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*\r\n\r\n### User Story 1 - Manager and Director approval authority (Priority: P1)\r\n\r\nA manager or director must be able to approve an invoice only when the invoice amount is within the authorized threshold for their role, and any invalid approval attempt must be rejected with a clear reason without changing the invoice state.\r\n\r\n**Why this priority**: This is the primary business workflow and the baseline rule for approval authority by role and amount.\r\n\r\n**Independent Test**: A manager can approve exactly 50,000 and a director can approve exactly 500,000, while amounts above those thresholds are rejected unless they satisfy the valid multi-approver rules.\r\n\r\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\r\n\r\n1. **Given** an invoice amount of 50,000 and a logged-in user with the Manager role, **When** the user approves the invoice, **Then** the approval succeeds and the invoice is marked approved.\r\n2. **Given** an invoice amount of 500,000 and a logged-in user with the Director role, **When** the user approves the invoice, **Then** the approval succeeds and the invoice is marked approved.\r\n3. **Given** an invoice amount above 50,000 and a logged-in user with the Manager role, **When** the user approves the invoice, **Then** the system rejects the request because Manager approvals are valid only up to and including 50,000 and the invoice remains unchanged.\r\n4. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a logged-in user with the Director role, **When** the user attempts approval without a valid second approver, **Then** the system rejects the attempt and the invoice remains unchanged.\r\n5. **Given** a logged-in user without a valid approval role, **When** the user attempts to approve an invoice, **Then** the system rejects the request with a clear authorization message and does not mutate the invoice.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### User Story 2 - Multi-approver enforcement for invoices above 500,000 (Priority: P1)\r\n\r\nAny invoice above 500,000 must have a valid two-step approval flow where the first approver is valid and the second approver is a distinct Director. The same person cannot approve twice, and invalid approval order must be rejected.\r\n\r\n**Why this priority**: This covers the highest-risk logic: two-approver enforcement, same-user rejection, and approval-order validation.\r\n\r\n**Independent Test**: An invoice above 500,000 can only be approved through a valid two-step flow where the second approver is a distinct Director.\r\n\r\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\r\n\r\n1. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the second approver is the same user, **Then** the system rejects the request and preserves the original invoice state.\r\n2. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the second approver is not a Director, **Then** the system rejects the request and preserves the original invoice state.\r\n3. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the approval order is invalid or the invoice is already finalized, **Then** the system rejects the request, returns a clear reason, and leaves the invoice unchanged.\r\n4. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and two valid approvers, **When** the request is processed successfully, **Then** the invoice is approved only after both approvers are distinct and the second approver is a Director.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### User Story 3 - Rejection integrity and state preservation (Priority: P1)\r\n\r\nWhen an approval or rejection request is invalid, the system must return a clear reason and must not partially update the invoice. A rejection requires a message, and the invoice must retain its previous state before the attempted approval decision.\r\n\r\n**Why this priority**: The assignment explicitly requires state integrity and reason-based rejection handling to prevent incorrect partial updates.\r\n\r\n**Independent Test**: A rejected approval or invalid rejection attempt leaves all invoice fields, status, and decision data unchanged, and a rejection without a message is rejected.\r\n\r\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\r\n\r\n1. **Given** an invoice awaiting decision and a user submits a rejection, **When** the rejection reason is blank, **Then** the system rejects the rejection and preserves the invoice state.\r\n2. **Given** a valid invoice and an invalid approval attempt, **When** the approval is rejected, **Then** the invoice remains exactly in its previous state and no partial decision data is written.\r\n3. **Given** a valid invoice before an attempted decision, **When** the user attempts approval or rejection with an invalid role, invalid order, duplicate approver, or already-finalized invoice, **Then** the system rejects the request and leaves the invoice unchanged.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### Edge Cases\r\n\r\n- What happens when the invoice amount is exactly 50,000 for a Manager approval?\r\n- What happens when the invoice amount is exactly 500,000 for a Director approval?\r\n- What happens when the invoice amount is just above 50,000 for a Manager approval?\r\n- What happens when the invoice amount is just above 500,000 for a Director approval?\r\n- What happens when the same user is listed twice in a two-approver approval sequence?\r\n- What happens when the second approver is not a Director?\r\n- What happens when approval is attempted on an already-approved or rejected invoice?\r\n- What happens when the rejection request includes no explanation message?\r\n- What happens when a failed approval occurs after the first approver is validated but before the invoice is persisted?\r\n## Requirements *(mandatory)*\r\n\r\n### Functional Requirements\r\n\r\n- **FR-001**: The system MUST allow a Manager to approve an invoice amount up to and including 50,000.\r\n- Multi-approver enforcement for invoices above 500,000 (Priority: P1)\r\n\r\nAny invoice above 500,000 must have a valid two-step approval flow where the first approver is valid and the second approver is a distinct Director. The same person cannot approve twice, and invalid approval order must be rejected.\r\n\r\n**Why this priority**: This covers the highest-risk logic: two-approver enforcement, same-user rejection, and approval-order validation.\r\n\r\n**Independent Test**: An invoice above 500,000 can only be approved through a valid two-step flow where the second approver is a distinct Director.\r\n\r\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\r\n\r\n1. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the second approver is the same user, **Then** the system rejects the request and preserves the original invoice state.\r\n2. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the second approver is not a Director, **Then** the system rejects the request and preserves the original invoice state.\r\n3. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the approval order is invalid or the invoice is already finalized, **Then** the system rejects the request, returns a clear reason, and leaves the invoice unchanged.\r\n4. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and two valid approvers, **When** the request is processed successfully, **Then** the invoice is approved only after both approvers are distinct and the second approver is a Director.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### User Story 3 - Rejection integrity and state preservation (Priority: P1)\r\n\r\nWhen an approval or rejection request is invalid, the system must return a clear reason and must not partially update the invoice. system MUST reject any approval sequence where the same user appears as both approvers.\r\n- **FR-008**: The system MUST reject invalid approval order, unsupported roles, and unauthorized attempts with a clear reason.\r\n- **FR-009**: The system MUST leave the invoice unchanged when any approval attempt is rejected, with no partial approval or state mutation.\r\n- **FR-010**: The system MUST sign-in.\r\n- **FR-012**: The approval rules MUST be implemented in the Domain layer, not in controllers, startup code, or the UI.\r\n- **FR-013**: The project MUST have automated tests covering threshold values, just-above thresholds, duplicate approvers, wrong role attempts, invalid order, already-finalized invoices, and invoice state integrity after rejected approvals.\r\n- **FR-014**: The validation, and test structure defined by the current project guidance.\r\n\r\n### Key Entities\r\n\r\n- **Invoice**: The approval target, including amount, status, actor metadata, and decision Understand the project first...\"\r\n\r\n## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*\r\n\r\n### User Story 1 - Manager and Director approval authority (Priority: P1)\r\n\r\nA manager or director must be able to approve an invoice only when the invoice amount is within the authorized threshold for their role, and any invalid approval attempt must be rejected with a clear reason without changing the invoice state.\r\n\r\n**Why this priority**: This is the primary business workflow and the baseline rule for approval authority by role and amount.\r\n\r\n**Independent Test**: A manager can approve exactly 50,000, and a director can independently approve any valid invoice amount up to and including 500,000, including amounts below 50,000. Attempts above the applicable single-approval limit are rejected without changing invoice state.\r\n\r\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\r\n\r\n1. **Given** an invoice amount of 50,000 and a logged-in user with the Manager role, **When** the user approves the invoice, **Then** the approval succeeds and the invoice is marked approved.\r\n2. **Given** an invoice amount of 500,000 or less and a logged-in user with the Director role, **When** the user approves the invoice, **Then** the approval succeeds and the invoice is marked approved.\r\n3. **Given** an invoice amount above 50,000 and a logged-in user with the Manager role, **When** the user approves the invoice, **Then** the system rejects the request because Manager approvals are valid only up to and including 50,000 and the invoice remains unchanged.\r\n4. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a logged-in user with the Director role, **When** the user attempts approval without a valid second approver, **Then** the system rejects the attempt and the invoice remains unchanged.\r\n5. **Given** a logged-in user without a valid approval role, **When** the user attempts to approve an invoice, **Then** the system rejects the request with a clear authorization message and does not mutate the invoice.\r\n6. **Given** an invoice amount greater than 50,000 and no greater than 500,000, and a logged-in Manager, **When** the Manager attempts approval through the actual user interface, **Then** the interface displays a clear rejection message, the invoice remains `PendingApproval`, and no final approval decision is recorded; this behavior MUST be verified by a Playwright end-to-end test.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### User Story 2 - Multi-approver enforcement for invoices above 500,000 (Priority: P1)\r\n\r\nAny invoice above 500,000 must have a valid two-step approval flow where the first approver is valid and the second approver is a distinct Director. The same person cannot approve twice, and invalid approval order must be rejected.\r\n\r\n**Why this priority**: This covers the highest-risk logic: two-approver enforcement, same-user rejection, and approval-order validation.\r\n\r\n**Independent Test**: An invoice above 500,000 can only be approved through a valid two-step flow where the second approver is a distinct Director.\r\n\r\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\r\n\r\n1. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the second approver is the same user, **Then** the system rejects the request and preserves the original invoice state.\r\n2. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the second approver is not a Director, **Then** the system rejects the request and preserves the original invoice state.\r\n3. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and a valid first approver, **When** the approval order is invalid or the invoice is already finalized, **Then** the system rejects the request, returns a clear reason, and leaves the invoice unchanged.\r\n4. **Given** an invoice amount above 500,000 and two valid approvers, **When** the request is processed successfully, **Then** the invoice is approved only after both approvers are distinct and the second approver is a Director.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### User Story 3 - Rejection integrity and state preservation (Priority: P1)\r\n\r\nWhen an approval or rejection request is invalid, the system must return a clear reason and must not partially update the invoice. A rejection requires a message, and the invoice must retain its previous state before the attempted approval decision.\r\n\r\n**Why this priority**: The assignment explicitly requires state integrity +
+    private static void EnsureApprovalAllowed(Invoice invoice, string role)
+    {
+        if (role == "Manager" && invoice.Amount <= 50_000m)
+        {
+            return;
+        }
+
+        if (role == "Director" && invoice.Amount <= 500_000m)
+        {
+            return;
+        }
+
+        var reason = role switch
+        {
+            "Manager" => "Managers may approve invoices only up to 50000.",
+            "Director" => "Directors may approve invoices only up to 500000 in a single approval.",
+            _ => $"Role '{role}' is not authorized to approve invoices.",
+        };
+
+        throw new InvalidOperationException(reason);
+    }
 }

+import { expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';
+
+export class InvoiceApprovalPage {
+  constructor(private readonly page: Page) {}
+
+  async open() {
+    await this.page.goto('/');
+  }
+
+  async signIn(username: string, password: string) {
+    await this.page.getByLabel('Username').fill(username);
+    await this.page.getByLabel('Password').fill(password);
+    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
+    await expect(this.page.getByText(`${username} (Manager)`)).toBeVisible();
+  }
+
+  async createAndSubmitInvoice(customerName: string, amount: number) {
+    await this.page.getByLabel('Customer name').fill(customerName);
+    await this.page.getByLabel('Amount').fill(String(amount));
+    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create invoice' }).click();
+
+    const invoiceRow = this.page
+      .getByRole('row')
+      .filter({ hasText: customerName });
+    await expect(invoiceRow).toBeVisible();
+    await invoiceRow
+      .getByRole('button', { name: /Submit invoice .* for approval/ })
+      .click();
+    await expect(invoiceRow.getByRole('cell').nth(3)).toHaveText('Pending Approval');
+    return invoiceRow.getByRole('cell').nth(0).innerText();
+  }
+
+  async approveAsManager(invoiceId: string) {
+    await this.page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Approvals' }).click();
+    await this.page
+      .getByRole('button', { name: `Approve invoice ${invoiceId}` })
+      .click();
+  }
+
+  async expectPendingApproval(invoiceId: string, customerName: string) {
+    await this.page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Invoices' }).click();
+    const invoiceRow = this.page
+      .getByRole('row')
+      .filter({ hasText: customerName });
+    await expect(invoiceRow.getByRole('cell').nth(3)).toHaveText('Pending Approval');
+
+    await this.page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Approvals' }).click();
+    const pendingInvoice = this.page
+      .getByRole('listitem')
+      .filter({ hasText: invoiceId });
+    await expect(pendingInvoice).toBeVisible();
+  }
+
+  async getAuthenticatedInvoice(invoiceId: string) {
+    const token = await this.page.evaluate(() => {
+      const session = JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem('session') ?? 'null');
+      return session?.token;
+    });
+
+    const response = await this.page.request.get(`/api/invoices/${invoiceId}`, {
+      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
+    });
+    expect(response.ok()).toBeTruthy();
+    return response.json();
+  }
+
+  async expectDecisionError(message: string) {
+    await expect(this.page.getByRole('alert').filter({ hasText: message })).toBeVisible();
+  }
+}

+import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';
+import { InvoiceApprovalPage } from '../pages/invoice-approval-page';
+
+test('Manager cannot approve an invoice above 50000 through the UI', async ({ page }) => {
+  const invoicePage = new InvoiceApprovalPage(page);
+  const customerName = `Manager limit check ${Date.now()}`;
+
+  await invoicePage.open();
+  await invoicePage.signIn('demo.manager', 'ChangeMe123!');
+  const invoiceId = await invoicePage.createAndSubmitInvoice(customerName, 50_001);
+
+  await invoicePage.approveAsManager(invoiceId);
+
+  await invoicePage.expectDecisionError('Managers may approve invoices only up to 50000.');
+  await invoicePage.expectPendingApproval(invoiceId, customerName);
+
+  const invoice = await invoicePage.getAuthenticatedInvoice(invoiceId);
+  expect(invoice.status).toBe('PendingApproval');
+  expect(invoice.decidedBy).toBeNull();
+  expect(invoice.decidedAt).toBeNull();
+});
